A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSPC research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A.1–A.6. Their equations, tables, figures, and experimental descriptions support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LSPC-S and LSPC-O benchmark results, ablations, and zero-shot MetaDrive transfer experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original LSPC benchmark results, ablations, and transfer experiments, including Tables 1 and 3–5 and Figure 12.

M1.justification: The CVAE safe-policy construction, IQL critics, reward-weighted latent encoder, latent restrictions, and training procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MetaDrive, Safety Gymnasium, and Bullet Safety Gym tasks, including the same MetaDrive transfer scenarios in Appendix A.6.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains BC-Safe, CDT, CPQ, and FISOR. Tables 3–5 retain the additional BC, BCQ-Lag, BEAR-Lag, and COptiDICE comparisons; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The reward/cost normalization, target cost thresholds, training settings, and transfer evaluation over 20 episodes remain unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Both retain the latent restriction, reversed architecture, inverse-temperature, and expectile-loss analyses in Figures 4–8, along with dataset safety profiles and zero-shot transfer analyses in Appendices A.5–A.6.

E5.justification: Both specify three random seeds for benchmark evaluation and retain the same uncertainty displays. No run-count disclosure, uncertainty estimation procedure, or statistical test is added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported numerical outcomes and plotted findings are unchanged. Table 1 removes a stray zero preceding BC-Safe's MediumSparse reward of 0.33; Table 3 already reports 0.33 in v1, establishing this as typographic cleanup of the same result.

T1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A.1–A.2 retain the same definitions, assumptions, performance and constraint-violation bounds, sample-complexity analysis, and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about latent safety constraints, reward optimization, theoretical guarantees, and empirical performance. The added code-access sentence does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The baseline interpretations, safety–reward trade-offs, transfer explanations, and limitations concerning latent-space restrictiveness remain unchanged, including Section 7 and Appendices A.3.3 and A.6.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code link in the abstract and footnote 1. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and dataset/baseline access information in Appendices A.3–A.4 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning against prior methods are unchanged. Reference movement following the new acknowledgments does not change bibliography membership.

P1.justification: v2 adds a brief code-availability sentence and NSF acknowledgments, and replaces the review-status header with an ICLR 2025 publication header. The scientific narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 replaces gray row shading with pale green/pink shading and removes a stray zero. The new footnote and acknowledgments cause limited text and reference reflow; figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The project-code pointer newly supplies useful reproducibility access information, and Table 1 receives a small typographic cleanup. These provide a limited practical improvement; the methods, evidence, theory, and appendix analyses remain unchanged.
